memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'If your grain offering is prepared on a griddle, it is to be made of the finest flour mixed with oil, and without yeast. Crumble it and pour oil on it; it is a grain offering.'" - Lev 2:5-6 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Crumble it. The bread the worshipper carefully prepared was to be broken into pieces before it was offered.

There is no explanation given, but there is a pattern here that runs right through Scripture. What is offered to God is often broken first. Jesus took bread, gave thanks, broke it, and said, "This is my body given for you" (Lk 22:19). The feeding of the five thousand happened through broken loaves. David wrote that a broken and contrite heart God will not despise (Ps 51:17).

That is not because God enjoys seeing things damaged. It is because whole, intact, self-sufficient things tend to stay in our own hands. What is broken can be shared, poured out, distributed.

If you are in a season where something in your life has been crumbled — plans, health, confidence, a relationship — do not assume God has set you aside. The griddle offering was still an offering. It was still received. Broken did not mean rejected.

And notice what happens after the crumbling: pour oil on it. The oil comes to the broken pieces. Throughout Scripture oil is associated with God's Spirit and His anointing. God does not abandon what has been broken open. He fills it.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What has been broken in my life that I have assumed disqualifies me?
2. Can I bring the crumbled pieces to God rather than hiding them?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, I bring You what is broken in me rather than pretending it is whole. Pour Your Spirit into these pieces and use them for Your glory. Amen.
